findings.reason: §32's done-when requires each of the 16 re-entered names to sit at "the stage from which the pipeline's name review claims them", so a node sent to a file that holds no such rule either guesses the stage or leaves it unstated, and the stage it picks is the graph write the section exists to make.
findings.text: §32 tells the node to read "the claim rule in `imas_codex/discovery/AGENTS.md` and in the standard-name pool code", but that file contains no `name_stage`, `StandardName` or `review` reference at all — it is the facility-path claim protocol (worker coordination, `claimed_at`, deadlock patterns); the rule it means is `REVIEW_NAME | name_stage='drafted'` in `imas_codex/core/AGENTS.md:23`

findings.reason: with no floor the node can close green having linked zero successors, and the single control row tests only that validation ran, not that any edge was written.
findings.text: §33's done-when measures "the adjudicated count admitted and its 1 control row refused", so a run that adjudicates none of the 14 and lists all 14 as unadjudicated satisfies the whole gate; the census §33 came from already fixes the targets for the 2 legacy spellings ("a signed successor edge to the canonical accepted identity"), so an adjudication floor exists and is not stated

findings.reason: the only argument distinguishing the 183 from the 25 rests on a mechanism the named policy does not run on them, and the section's "stop if the split has moved" checkpoint re-reads the counts, not the rationale, so a wrong rationale is not caught downstream.
findings.text: §31 justifies keeping the 183 superseded rather than taking the census's reclassification remedy with "a name with no producing source would be retired again by the orphan lifecycle policy on its next pass", but the policy that writes `supersede_exhausted_orphan` claims `name_stage = 'exhausted' AND NOT EXISTS {(:StandardNameSource)-[:PRODUCED_NAME]->(name)}` (`imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:22613`), so a name already at `superseded` is never re-claimed and no "next pass" retires it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §32 points the node at `imas_codex/discovery/AGENTS.md` for the name-review claim rule, but that file holds no standard-name content; the rule it needs is in `imas_codex/core/AGENTS.md`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §33's done-when accepts any adjudicated count, including zero, and its single control row guards only against a silently-skipped validation, not against a node that links nothing.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every authority and fragment §31–§33 write lands in `docs/evidence/fragments/sn-integrity-backlog/` beside the §30 census, a committed path, and no gate reads from a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, comment or new code path; the `sib-` fragment ids follow the evidence-archive convention the sibling fragments already use and are artifact names, not code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §31 justifies keeping the 183 superseded with an orphan policy whose claim predicate is `exhausted`, so it would not retire an already-`superseded` name.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §31 records the 183 orphan retirements, §32 restores the 25 still-produced names, §33 links the 14 names that lost their successor; one class and one treatment each.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §31 declares the three-way split of the 208 (183 recorded / 25 restored / 14 linked) and names §32 and §33 as the sections taking the other two classes; s31–s33 carry no relationship attributes in the composed surface, and none of the three names a dependency the plan does not otherwise define.
